children: India’s gold imports nearly matched the country’s entire gems and jewellery exports in August, a sharp monthly shift with implications for the trade balance, even as cumulative imports of the metal remain higher than the previous year.

This shift comes after the government raised the effective gold import duty from 6 percent to 15 percent on May 13, comprising a 10 percent basic customs duty and a 5 percent Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess.
India imported gold worth $2.30 billion in August, down nearly 58 percent from $5.44 billion a year earlier, according to government data.
The country’s merchandise trade deficit sharply narrowed from $31.98 billion in July to $26.86 billion in August as gold imports nearly halved.

At the same time, gross gems and jewellery exports rose 3.14 percent year-on-year to $2.30 billion, according to the Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC). With the import and export figures virtually equal, it created a near-exact 1:1 ratio.

The parity narrowed the foreign-exchange gap between gold imports and jewellery exports. With both at $2.30 billion, the two flows were effectively balanced, compared with a $1.81 billion gap in July. This implies a lower net foreign-exchange outflow from these two components but does not by itself indicate a change in the overall balance of payments.
In July, gold imports were $4.16 billion, while gems and jewellery exports were at $2.35 billion, a gap of about $1.81 billion. Gold imports were 1.77 times the value of the exports.
Gold imports have been volatile in recent months. Shipments initially fell to around $1.97 billion in June before more than doubling in July and again falling to $2.30 billion in August.
The July surge came amid inventory replenishment ahead of the festival season, while the August decline brought imports much closer to the June level.
Despite the sharp August fall, the cumulative picture is different.
Gold imports during April-August rose 3.38 percent YoY to $17.47 billion. Gross gems and jewellery exports during the period rose 2.58 percent to $11.47 billion, GJEPC data shows.
That leaves a cumulative gap of about $6 billion, with gold imports roughly 1.52 times the value of gems and jewellery exports.
The August 1:1 ratio is, therefore, a monthly development rather than a reflection of the year-to-date position.

The decline in gold imports also helped moderate India’s merchandise import bill in August. Total merchandise imports stood at $70.67 billion, while merchandise exports reached $43.81 billion, leaving a trade deficit of $26.86 billion.
For April-August, however, the merchandise trade deficit was $147.09 billion, compared with $123.88 billion a year earlier.
The gems and jewellery sector’s headline growth also masked differences across categories.

Studded gold jewellery exports surged 51.22 percent to $642.85 million in August, supporting overall sector exports. Cut-and-polished diamond exports remained under pressure in value terms even as shipment volumes rose 3.23 percent year-on-year to 13.36 lakh carats.

Other value-added categories performed better during the April-August period. Polished lab-grown diamond exports rose 11.75 percent to $533.67 million, silver jewellery increased 35.57 percent to $594.86 million and platinum jewellery exports climbed 19.67 percent to $100.32 million.
The broader export picture was considerably stronger.
India’s merchandise exports jumped to $43.81 billion in August from $34.74 billion a year earlier.
For April-August, exports reached $215.91 billion, up form $183.21 billion in the previous year.

title: India’s gold imports nearly match entire gems and jewellery exports in August
